**UK competition authority proposes opening Apple's NFC chip to rivals**

*The proposed remedies would lower fees and remove technical barriers for Apple Pay competitors, with the FCA framing NFC access as a prerequisite for expanding open banking at the point of sale.*

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has published proposals to unlock contactless payment technology on iPhones, requiring Apple to give rival payment providers access to its NFC chip on fair terms. The consultation sets out measures to reduce the fees Apple charges for NFC access and to remove technical restrictions that have kept competitors off the platform.

David Geale, the Financial Conduct Authority's executive director for payments and digital finance, said that opening up the technology would support the expansion of open banking by enabling more people to make payments directly from their bank accounts. That framing positions NFC access not just as a competition issue between wallet providers but as infrastructure for pay-by-bank at physical points of sale, where open banking has so far had negligible presence.

The proposals follow the CMA's market investigation into mobile payments, which found Apple's control of NFC access on iOS restricted competition. Apple has argued that its restrictions protect user security and privacy. The consultation is open until November 17, after which the CMA will decide whether to impose binding remedies.

*Sources: [UK sets out proposal to open up access to iPhone contactless payments](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48618/uk-sets-out-proposal-to-open-up-access-to-iphone-contactless-payments?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra | [Apple should open access to contactless payment systems, says regulator](https://www.standard.co.uk/news/tech/nfc-apple-pay-fca-press-association-b1301591.html) — The Standard | [CMA outlines proposals to unlock contactless technology on Apple iPhone](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/cma-outlines-proposals-to-unlock-contactless-technology-on-apple-iphone/) — Openbankingexpo*

**Visa runs first live agentic payment between buyer and supplier platforms**

*Moving agentic commerce from consumer experiments into accounts payable, the pilot with Bill and Billtrust marks the first production test of AI agents completing end-to-end B2B invoice payments.*

AI agents are now initiating and completing approved buyer invoice payments end-to-end through supplier portals in a live pilot between Visa, Bill and Billtrust. The pilot is the first to move agentic payments into a production B2B environment, where agents handle the full cycle from invoice receipt to payment execution without manual intervention.

The pilot sits within a rapidly filling competitive space. Mastercard, ING, Blik, GoCardless and Credit Agricole have all completed agentic payment transactions in recent months, but those have largely been consumer or proof-of-concept exercises. Visa's move into accounts payable targets a segment where automation has obvious economic value: B2B invoice processing remains manual at many firms, and the potential to reduce processing costs is substantial.

The deployment also tests trust and authorisation frameworks in a higher-stakes context than consumer purchases. B2B payments involve larger values, multi-party approval chains and contractual obligations, making the governance model around agent permissions more consequential than in retail settings.

*Sources: [Visa pilots AI agent payments between buyer and supplier platforms](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48610/visa-pilots-ai-agent-payments-between-buyer-and-supplier-platforms?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Criminals exploit open banking APIs to verify stolen card and bank credentials**

*Open banking's account verification services are being exploited as a free, low-friction method for fraudsters to check whether stolen credentials are valid before monetising them.*

Criminals have begun using open banking services as a cost-free way to test whether stolen bank and card details are valid, according to a report from Cybersecurity News. The technique exploits the account verification and balance-check capabilities that open banking APIs provide, allowing attackers to confirm credentials without triggering the transaction-monitoring systems that would flag a conventional card test at a merchant.

Traditional credential-testing methods — making small purchases or donations — carry costs and leave traces. Open banking's read-only account information services, by contrast, require only that the attacker has enough data to pass authentication. Where stolen credentials include sufficient identity information to initiate a consent flow, attackers can verify account validity silently. According to Cybersecurity News, the technique is being combined with phishing campaigns impersonating the retailer Poshmark.

Open banking's account information APIs represent an expanding attack surface that consent and authentication models were not designed to defend against adversarial use. Open Banking Limited published data on July 8 showing open banking fraud rates sit below wider UK payment benchmarks, but that analysis focused on payment initiation rather than the account information side. As open banking scales, assumptions about the channel's security relative to card payments will face increasing scrutiny.

*Sources: [Hackers Exploit Open Banking Services to Test Stolen Credentials Without Paying a Cent](https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-exploit-open-banking-services/) — Cybersecuritynews*

**Evervault launches token framework to secure agentic commerce transactions**

*Developers building AI agent commerce tools now have a way to handle payments and sensitive data without exposing credentials to the agent or browser provider, addressing a core trust gap in the emerging agentic stack.*

Evervault has launched Browser Tokens, a product that allows AI agents and browser automations to make purchases, log into accounts and complete sensitive workflows without exposing payment cards, passwords or personal data to the agent or the browser provider. The launch, announced at Money20/20, targets developers building agentic commerce products who need a secure intermediary between the AI agent and the payment credential.

The product sits in a gap that the payments industry has been circling for months. EMVCo drafted a framework for card-based agentic payments in September; Visa, Mastercard and others have launched agentic pilots; and JPMorgan moved in October to block outside AI agents from accessing customer accounts entirely. Each response reflects the same underlying problem: existing authentication and authorisation models assume a human is present. Evervault's approach tokenises the sensitive data so the agent never handles it directly, keeping the trust boundary between the AI and the financial system.

The question of whether Browser Tokens or a competing approach becomes the standard infrastructure layer remains open, but the product illustrates a clear market forming around agentic trust infrastructure. For payment providers and issuers, ensuring AI agents transact within a controllable security perimeter is now the focus rather than whether they will transact at all.

*Sources: [Evervault launches Browser Tokens, enabling secure agentic payments](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/111376/evervault-launches-browser-tokens-enabling-secure-agentic-payments?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
